subject: Bridge: Hosted API sudden degradation — Pegasus AI production impact
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@pegasusai.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example
Cc: ops@pegasusai.com
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors / high latency on Redwood Hosted API

Ben —

We started seeing a significant spike in inference latency and a flurry of 5xx errors hitting our production traffic at ~07:50 PDT. p95 is up ~3x and p99s are in the multi-second range; customers on our end are losing responses. This coincided with a sharp increase in error rates in our online flows.

Attached are a couple of traces and a Grafana screenshot showing the tail latency around the time window. Our ops team also captured a set of Kubernetes events (attached).

We need immediate remediation — can we get a bridge and an estimate for impact and mitigations? This is affecting our enterprise customers and the renewal conversation is sensitive.

Sandeep Rao
Head of Platform, Pegasus AI
ops@pegasusai.com

Attachments: pegasus-traces-20271005.json (text), grafana-screenshot-latency.png (image)
From: ben_carter@redwood.example <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@pegasusai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, marcus_lin@redwood.example, diego_fernandez@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors / high latency on Redwood Hosted API

Thanks for flagging, Sandeep — I’m very sorry for the disruption. We’re standing a triage bridge now. Marcus (runtime lead) and Diego (ops) are on immediate rotation. Laura, I’ll need an executive summary for Pegasus leadership within 90 minutes.

Action so far (we’ve started these):
- Spun up a temporary burst pool in us-west to relieve capacity pressure.
- Routed Pegasus traffic to the burst pool to reduce queueing.
- Captured host-level metrics and kernel traces; Marcus taking point on analysis.

Propose 8:30am PDT bridge (Zoom link in related_links) — can you confirm?

Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: marcus_lin@redwood.example <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors / high latency on Redwood Hosted API

Bridge notes / initial findings:

Summary: we’re seeing a cluster of GPU memory OOMs and repeated slab fragmentation on several Triton-hosted nodes serving Pegasus model variants. The symptomatic signal: frequent small evictions in the KV cache followed by full allocator compactions that spike tail latency. There are correlated logs showing repeated "OOM: cudaMalloc failed" and GPU driver warnings around 07:48–07:56.

Evidence:
- Attachments: k8s-events-20271005.log includes pod restarts on node gpu-usw-17.
- Sample trace in pegasus-traces points to stalls during KV cache reseed and weight-swap ops (sequence id 9k7x).
- Memory fragmentation appears worse on older ultra32 instances with mixed-quantized model variants.

Immediate mitigations enacted:
1) Fail traffic to a compatible but slightly lower-capacity model pool (maintains correctness, lowers peak memory pressure).
2) Recycled a small subset of affected nodes (preventative reboot) and removed them from rotation.
3) Increased continuous batching threshold temporarily to smooth allocations (short-term latency tradeoff).

Next steps (short):
- Marcus to run a compact/defrag routine on spare nodes and test model startup memory behaviour (ETA 45m).
- Diego to verify autoscaler headroom and hold burst pool until tail stabilizes.
- Ben/Laura to coordinate exec comms and customer compensation if needed.

Marcus Lin
Runtime Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.example <diego_fernandez@redwood.example>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example, marcus_lin@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors / high latency on Redwood Hosted API

Operational update:
- Burst pool absorbed ~40% of Pegasus peak load within 10 mins of reroute; error rate dropped by ~60% for routed requests.
- Recycled 4 nodes from gpu-usw-17 (warm restart) — node telemetry shows memory curvature returning to nominal.
- Queue depth at the inference gateway reduced after temporary batching bump; overall p95 trending down but p99 still elevated on a small request subset (large context and multi-tool calls).

I’ve attached the k8s events and a short dump with the driver warnings for Marcus. We should keep the burst pool for at least 2 hours as a safety net while Marcus runs the mem-defrag tests.

Diego Fernandez
Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: k8s-events-20271005.log (text)
From: ben_carter@redwood.example <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@pegasusai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, marcus_lin@redwood.example, diego_fernandez@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-bridge summary and exec next steps — Pegasus incident (08:30 PDT bridge)

Sandeep — thank you for joining the bridge this morning. Below is a concise summary for your execs and our internal leadership.

What happened:
- Starting ~07:48 PDT there was a sudden change in allocation patterns on a subset of GPU nodes serving Pegasus model variants. Repeated small-kernel allocations caused fragmentation and intermittent cudaMalloc failures leading to OOMs and pod restarts for a narrow portion of requests (large-context, multi-tool flows). This manifested as p95/p99 regressions and higher 5xx rates.

Immediate impact and mitigation (completed):
- Rerouted Pegasus traffic to a burst pool to reduce queueing (reduced visible error rates by ~60%).
- Recycled affected nodes and quarantined a small cohort until compact/defrag verification.
- Temporarily adjusted batching to smooth allocations (minor p95 increase but reduced p99 spikes).

Short-term plan (next 72h):
- Marcus to run targeted memory compaction/allocator tuning on affected instance types and validate under load (~T+6–12h validation window).
- Ops to hold burst pool active until validated and to add additional warm capacity in us-west as a buffer.
- Product & Accounts: we’ll coordinate a customer-facing incident writeup and discuss credits if net SLA breach is likely. Ben & Laura to prepare comms.

Longer-term fixes under investigation:
- Kernel selection and allocator changes to reduce fragmentation for mixed-quantized models.
- Improved early-warning telemetry for small-allocation churn and a replay harness for reproducing KV cache reseed stalls.
- Consider an automated fallback routing policy for model-variant memory-pressure conditions.

Requested exec asks (for leadership):
1) Approve 24/7 extended burst capacity funding for peak-critical customers for the next 30 days (to be used as safety net during rollout).
2) Fast-track a small reliability charter (2 sprints) for allocator and compaction work (Marcus to scope).
3) If SLA credits are needed, allow Accounts to negotiate with Pegasus on a case-by-case basis (Ben/Laura will propose amounts).

We’ll send a customer-facing timeline and a technical post-mortem once the mem-defrag validation finishes. Please let me know if Pegasus wants a dedicated follow-up with our CTO.

Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199
